subject: Order form redlines: conditional net terms, tax reserve & SLA language
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Soto <ana.soto@nimbus.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form redlines: conditional net terms, tax reserve & SLA language

Hi Ana / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — good alignment on scope and expected usage patterns. Attached is Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx with our initial set of redlines called out on the pricing schedule, minimum commits, and invoicing path. A couple of open items we want to close with you before legal/finance exchanges final counters: 

- Net terms: your procurement note requested Net 45. Redwood standard is Net 30. We're open to a conditional Net 45 for the first invoice(s) provided we receive a PO and the billing entity passes a quick credit check. Can you confirm your internal PO timing and whether Nimbus can accept split invoicing if we need to route invoices to two entities?
- Minimum commit: the draft includes a 6‑month minimum ramp. We proposed a staged activation (25% first invoice, remainder over next 90 days). If Nimbus needs a lower ramp for year one, state target so we can quantify pricing bands.
- Taxes/withholding: please provide the VAT registration or W‑8/W‑9 equivalent for the payer entity. If withholding is required in your jurisdiction, we need to discuss either gross‑up language or an invoice withholding allowance clause (recommended approach below).
- SLA credits / service termination: legal asked us to limit SLA credits to a percentage of affected invoice(s); do you have any non‑negotiables for SLA language?

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx (order form with comments).

Can we do a 30‑minute sync Thursday to run through the PO/tax and settle the net terms language so legal can publish a single redline? Proposed times: Thu 1/12 10:00 or 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0124

[attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx]

From: Ana Soto <ana.soto@nimbus.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: conditional net terms, tax reserve & SLA language

Marcus — thanks, got the doc and shared with procurement. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) PO timing & invoice routing: Nimbus procurement can issue a PO within 7–10 business days once commercial terms are signed. We do need the option to route invoices to our European operating company for VAT purposes for any EU usage. That means we may ask for entity split in invoicing. Is Redwood able to split invoices by entity with a single order form?

2) Net terms: Net 45 would be our standard. We can be flexible on a staged approach (Net 45 first invoice, Net 30 after two paid invoices) but we need that documented. If Redwood requires credit checks in lieu of extended terms, can you confirm what data you need from us?

3) Tax documents: procurement attached our billing requirements and a copy of the VAT registration for the EU entity. See attachment: Nimbus_PO_requirements.pdf. We will push for no gross‑up (our treasury prefers withholding rather than grossing).

4) SLA: our legal has one ask — SLA credits should be available as an offset against future invoices rather than refunds.

We can take the call Thu 1/12 14:00 PT. I'll loop in our legal if we get close on wording.

Best,
Ana Soto
Procurement Manager, Nimbus Technologies
ana.soto@nimbus.com | +1 212 555 0199

[attachment: Nimbus_PO_requirements.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: conditional net terms, tax reserve & SLA language

Marcus / team — quick internal note before the Thu sync. I reviewed Ana's procurement response and the attached PO requirements. High level recommendations for the redline we should send to Nimbus: 

- Net terms compromise: add a conditional Net 45 clause that reads: "Seller may invoice on Net 45 for the initial two invoices provided Buyer issues a bona fide purchase order and Seller completes a standard credit check. Thereafter, invoices shall be Net 30 unless otherwise agreed in writing." This protects Redwood while giving Nimbus runway.

- Entity invoicing: add a Billing Appendix that allows for invoice routing to multiple entities by invoice number with a single order form reference. Require Buyer to supply Tax IDs and the billing entity per invoice. That will solve VAT routing without changing the primary payer undertakings.

- Withholding and gross‑up: do not accept a general gross‑up. Instead add a withholding clause that requires Buyer to: (i) notify Seller in advance of any withholding; (ii) provide official withholding documentation and certificates; and (iii) make reasonable efforts to secure a tax credit. If Buyer insists on gross‑up we can allow a limited gross‑up for withholdings >10% subject to cap and mitigation.

- Tax reserve / escrow: propose a 5% escrow holdback in the case of outstanding tax evidence for the first 60 days after invoicing, released upon submission of valid tax documentation. This is our recommended defense against retroactive VAT liabilities.

- SLA credits: accept offset versus refunds, but cap cumulative SLA credits per month to 30% of the monthly invoice for service‑credit events. Keep explicit exclusion for force majeure and scheduled maintenance.

I attached a short PDF with tracked language for the Net Terms and Withholding paragraphs (redlines_markus_20280111.pdf). If Marcus can present the conditional Net 45 + escrow compromise on Thu, that should get us over the line. Laura — FYI on the escrow holdback (will require Finance signoff if accepted).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

[attachment: redlines_markus_20280111.pdf]

Ana — appreciate the quick turn. Per our call and internal legal/finance review, attached is Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redlined.docx with the compromise language baked in. Summary of key points and next steps: 

1) Net terms: we will accept Net 45 for the first two invoices conditional on (a) purchase order; and (b) satisfactory credit check. After two consecutive paid invoices, the standard Net 30 will apply. If Nimbus prefers Net 30 from execution, we can offer a 2% early payment discount.

2) Invoice routing / entity split: added Billing Appendix A to support per‑invoice entity designation. Please confirm the payer entity and provide the VAT/TIN for that entity when you return the countersigned order form.

3) Tax reserve: implemented a 5% tax reserve / escrow holdback for disputed VAT or missing tax evidence, released within 60 days upon receipt of valid documentation. This is consistent with what Kimberly recommended.

4) SLA credits: accepted as credit against future invoices with monthly cap of 30% of the monthly invoice. Exclusions for scheduled maintenance remain.

Next steps: 
- I attached the redlined Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redlined.docx). If this looks acceptable, please confirm and we'll issue a DocuSign envelope for countersignature: https://www.docusign.com/tx/ABC1234567890
- HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2027-1098-NIM

If you want, we can include a short one‑page billing appendix that procurement signs off on to make routing operationally straightforward. Otherwise, if you confirm the PO and the payer entity today we can start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.
